post.caption: Queen Elizabeth's pearls carried a message. In her portraits, pearls symbolized her chastity. The Armada Portrait, painted around 1588, is full of pearls, and its pearls link her to Cynthia, the Greek goddess of the Moon. Another portrait ties her pearls to Diana, also a moon goddess. In 1568 she bought the pearls of Mary, Queen of Scots, before Catherine de' Medici of France could. Her 1587 inventory of jewels lists 628 pieces, and on New Year's Day 1587 she received more than 80 pieces. In the Ditchley portrait of about 1592, pearls cluster on her buttons.
